Prepare and trim raw DNA sequences

Source: R/parse.R
rb_sequence_prep.Rd

Utility functions for preparing raw DNA sequences during source standardization.

  • rb_reverse_complement(): Returns the reverse complement of a DNA sequence.

  • rb_remove_primers(): Removes matching forward and reverse primer sequences from the ends of a sequence, if present.

Usage

rb_reverse_complement(dna_seq)

rb_remove_primers(
  sequence,
  f_primer_seqs = NA_character_,
  r_primer_seqs = NA_character_
)

Arguments

dna_seq

Character vector of DNA sequences.

sequence

Character vector of DNA sequences to trim.

f_primer_seqs

Character vector of forward primer sequences. Use NA if no forward primers should be removed.

r_primer_seqs

Character vector of reverse primer sequences. Use NA if no reverse primers should be removed.

Value

A character vector of transformed sequences.

Details

rb_remove_primers() performs simple exact matching at sequence ends. Forward primers are removed from the start of the sequence. Reverse primers are reverse-complemented and removed from the end of the sequence.

See also

Other parsing: rb_ambiguity_utils, rb_combine_resolve, rb_parse_sources

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
rb_reverse_complement("ATGC")

rb_remove_primers(
  "ACGTACGTACGT",
  f_primer_seqs = "ACGT",
  r_primer_seqs = NA
)
} # }
